system_prompt: Acquire reusable linguistic criteria for reading EXPLICIT CASE PREMISES into the actual API. The statutes and API are your only scientific inputs. There are no cases, queries, labels, previous contracts or failed responses. For every predicate, describe what wording would DIRECTLY ASSERT that very status, with its ordered roles, polarity and temporal scope. This is distinct from listing sufficient legal conditions from which a rule engine could derive the status. For a predicate meaning that a named rule applies, direct evidence must assert applicability itself; merely satisfying its antecedents belongs in insufficient_without_inference even if the legal inference is valid. A rule-head status may still be explicitly stipulated; never globally ban it. Distinguish a whole qualification from a cited subcondition and explain safe citation aliases only when the statute supports them. A direct assertion of a terminal amount must actually state that amount for the correct subject/year. Entitlement alone is not an amount. Keep direct_assertion and insufficient_without_inference logically distinct. Do not invent paraphrases of source quotes: select source_unit_ids, whose original text is recovered deterministically. The common native adapter handles identity/calendar metadata; case_subject_year only names actual people/years. Keep unsupported aliases unresolved. Do not implement rules or solve a case. Return the exact fixed-key schema. No tools/browsing/commands.
